prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.meaning: Nidagha tells Ribhu that his mind runs here and there, restless and pointless, wandering far away like a stray dog in a village. He is young and back from a long pilgrimage, and he feels life slipping through his fingers. He says the mind will not stay still, it craves everything, and mastering it feels harder than drinking the ocean. The verse says that naming this wandering is the first step. It is not about forcing the mind to stop, but about seeing where it goes and how it runs after every sound.
verse.for_you: You have been scrolling for seven hours, and the mind is still running. The phone is the stray dog, and it keeps running because it has not found one place to land.

verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.

verse.line: Like a lamp in a windless place that doesn't flicker: that's a settled mind.
verse.translation: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker: that is the image used for the yogi of controlled mind practising union with the self.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna is showing Arjuna what a settled mind looks like while teaching him to meditate. He says the mind of someone who is steady and united with the self is like a lamp in a place with no wind. It does not flicker. The image is simple. A flame needs a calm place to burn without shaking. That calm place is the mind that has learned to rest in one direction, and the wind is the noise that pulls it apart.
verse.for_you: Your phone is the wind. The screen keeps pulling your mind into different directions before it can settle. You do not have to stop the wind. You only have to give your attention one place to land, and let it rest there for a moment.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.meaning: Krishna answers Arjuna about what a steady person is like. He says when a person draws their senses back from what pulls at them, their wisdom is firmly set. He uses the image of a tortoise. A tortoise pulls its limbs into its shell when it feels danger. It does not fight the world. It simply makes itself small and safe. The limbs are the senses, and the shell is the mind. When the senses are pulled back, anger and sorrow have nothing to feed on.
verse.for_you: Your mind is scattered because it is reaching out to every notification and every thought. Today, pull back one sense. Put the phone in another room for one hour. Let your mind become the shell. See what happens when nothing new is allowed to pull at it.

prasang.title: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals
prasang.summary: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
prasang.lesson: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells Rama that daily practice and clear thinking make the mind clear, slowly, the way a mango ripens. He is explaining that effort and grace are not rivals, that steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango, and that the mind ripens into its sweetness by itself.
verse.for_you: Your mind is like a mango that is not yet ripe. Instead of forcing it, keep the daily practice of bringing your attention back, even for a few minutes. Let the phone stay on the table while you do that one thing. The sweetness will come on its own.

anchor.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
anchor.translation: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.

script: Your mind will not settle. You are studying but the thoughts keep moving. Your phone is open and the hours pass. It feels like the thoughts are driving you, not the other way around.
Arjuna stands before Krishna. He has tried to find peace but his mind keeps jumping. He tells Krishna that the mind is hard to hold. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

The mind is strong and stubborn. It wants to go everywhere. Trying to force it still only makes it fight back. But practice and letting go can train it. You do not break the mind. You teach it where to rest.

For you, today. Your mind feels restless and scattered right now. The phone gives it a place to run, but it does not give it a place to rest. This verse says the mind is strong and stubborn, but it can be trained. Let it be what it is, and give it one small place to land.

depth.life: Your mind is scattered right now. You are studying, but the phone pulls you in for seven hours. The thoughts keep jumping, and nothing feels settled.
depth.points: The mind is stubborn and strong. It will not be forced into stillness. It needs a place to land, not a fight.
depth.practice: Put the phone down for five minutes. Look at one spot in the room. Let the thoughts move. Do not push them away.
depth.question: What happens to the noise when you stop feeding it?
